says: Today's lead tooling: loosening.sh's properties() counts only fc.property and fc.asyncProperty calls, and its numRuns check reads only fast-check's numRuns key, so a law moved to it.prop or it.effect.prop, the shape decision 0579 asks for, is reported as a removed law with fewer numRuns even when it keeps its title, its checks and its run count.
proof: `sh .agents/skills/lead/scripts/loosening.sh e9988e259 5152cf3f8` on PR 1619 prints `removed law: P1 and P2: owed work stays owed ...` and `fewer numRuns: line 33` for next/packages/libfabrika/src/runtime/Owed.test.ts, whose law keeps its exact title and its runsFor({ fast: 20, full: 100 }) count, now passed as `{ arbitrary: { runs } }` to it.effect.prop; `rg -n 'prop' .agents/skills/lead/scripts/loosening.sh` finds no it.prop or arbitrary.runs case.
cost: Every 0579 move becomes a hand check of hits that are not loosening, so a real loosening in the same diff is easier to miss among them, and a law that drops its property for a plain example reads the same as a clean move.
